name: Jacobin
summary: Jacobinism is the revolutionary republicanism of the Jacobin Club and its Montagnard leaders, above all Robespierre. It held that sovereignty lies in the people and is indivisible, that a centralised republic should be defended by civic virtue and, in crisis, by terror, and that property and wealth should serve the public good without abolishing private ownership.
scope: The Montagnard Jacobins of 1793-94 around Robespierre and Saint-Just, based on Robespierre's 1793 declaration of rights and 1794 report on political morality, the Constitution of 1793 and reference accounts. Excludes the pre-1792 constitutional monarchist club, Girondins, and later uses of 'Jacobin' for any centralist.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The 1793 Constitution added a right to public assistance, which supports state-guaranteed care for those in need.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The Jacobin maximum also capped wages, so there is no clear stance; inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Generally pro-market in principle, but the Jacobins imposed general price maxima and requisitions when markets failed in wartime.

public-ownership.rationale: No program of nationalizing industries; wartime state direction was an emergency measure.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Robespierre proposed exempting those below subsistence and progressive taxation by size of fortune.

unions-good.rationale: The republic recognised citizens, not corporate bodies, and capped wages; inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: The 1793 Constitution guaranteed property, yet Robespierre limited it by the duty to respect others' rights and the right to existence.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred from state control of commerce as a source of public wealth.

cut-welfare.rationale: The 1793 Constitution recognised public assistance as a social debt.

worker-ownership.rationale: Robespierre called community of goods a chimera; wide property for individuals, not collective ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The Law of Suspects authorised detention on vague suspicion in defence of the Republic.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; no basis to infer a position.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Speech against the Republic was prosecuted as counterrevolutionary, though hate speech as such was not the issue.

strong-leader.rationale: Rule was by committees of the Convention, and Robespierre cast his rule as virtue serving the people, not a personal leader bypassing it.

state-harmful.rationale: Jacobinism centres on a sovereign, indivisible public authority over civil society.

limit-guns.rationale: The levee en masse and citizen armies relied on an armed people; inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: A strong security apparatus and army defended the Republic; inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Republican virtue was central to Jacobin politics; inferred.

rehabilitation.rationale: Terror was justice that is prompt, severe and inflexible.

traditional-family.rationale: Republican civic morality in Rousseau's mould was conventional about family; women excluded from the club; inferred.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed in Jacobin sources, so no position can be reliably inferred from their principles.

abortion-legal.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed in Jacobin sources, so no position can be reliably inferred from their principles.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The 1793 Constitution barred interference in other governments.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Inequality blamed on institutions rather than population, as in Robespierre's speech.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Revolutionary force and terror were defended as justice against enemies of liberty.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The Law of Suspects and Revolutionary Tribunal set aside ordinary protections, and Robespierre defended terror as prompt, severe justice.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The Law of the General Maximum fixed grain and staple prices and was enforced by revolutionary armies.

party-controls-media.rationale: Revolutionary government curbed the press in the Terror, but this was done by the state and Convention, not a ruling party; inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: The armies answered to the Convention and Committee of Public Safety through representatives on mission, not to the Club as such; inferred.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Jacobin universalism and the brotherhood of peoples favor welcoming foreigners to citizenship; the period had no stated rule on waiting, inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Jacobin republican virtue condemned officials enriching themselves and favored austere public service; no pay rule is stated, so inferred from Robespierre's rhetoric.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The Jacobin Club enforced a unified line through purges of members, and Robespierre required unity behind the Committee of Public Safety.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Jacobins held sovereignty to be indivisible and rested in the people of the single French republic, so a binding supranational body contradicts it.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Jacobins ruled through the Convention and its committees, and opposed monarchic executive power, with the 1793 Constitution placing the executive under the legislature.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The Jacobin line favored the Civil Constitution of the Clergy with elected clergy and later de-Christianization and the Cult of the Supreme Being, against episcopal authority.

clerical-rule.rationale: Jacobins were anticlerical republicans who placed sovereignty in the people and replaced church authority with civic cults.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Jacobins ran the revolutionary war effort, with the levee en masse and the defense of the nation as their first duty.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Robespierre made civic virtue the foundation of the republic, and the Jacobins used festivals, theatre control and censorship to shape republican morals.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Jacobins had no president, and the 1793 Constitution used annual legislative elections; no doctrine addresses re-election of a head of state.

recall-officials.rationale: Popular sovereignty and the right to insurrection imply that the people can discipline their representatives; the 1793 Constitution held its legislators accountable by annual elections, so this is inferred.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Revolutionary France's 1793 constitution renounced wars of conquest and alliances with tyrants; inferred as a rejection of permanent entangling alliances.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Robespierre limited property and favored a wide distribution of it, but did not abolish rent or private ownership.

people-in-arms.rationale: The levee en masse and the 1793 constitution's right of insurrection and civic armed duty favored a citizen-army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Robespierre's civic virtue was rooted in the simple, honest people and the republic of small property owners; inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Jacobins stressed a single indivisible republic of France, but they did not address divided nations as such.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Jacobins were largely educated lawyers and praised the people's virtue, but not as against the educated; inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Jacobins held a universalist civilising mission of the republic and Enlightenment progress over cultural relativism; inferred.

death-penalty.rationale: The Terror used execution on a vast scale against enemies of the republic, and Robespierre defended it as justice.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Jacobin republican education was to form virtuous citizens, but sex education and gender equality were not Jacobin aims; anachronistic, and women were excluded from politics.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The Jacobins promoted a civic cult of the Supreme Being and Enlightenment reason, and rejected church doctrine in education.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The Jacobin republic of virtue was austere and moralising, so it would likely restrict obscenity; anachronistic and inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The French republic treated citizens as made by the political community and grew citizenship by law, not by descent alone.

minority-language-support.rationale: The indivisible republic imposed French on the regions, and the Convention in 1794 decreed French as the sole language.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Robespierre and the Jacobins demanded a unified law for all citizens and policed religion as a threat to republican unity.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Jacobin civic virtue demanded conformity to republican values; eccentricity was suspect in the Terror.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The Jacobins did not address foreign debts of poor countries; the issue is anachronistic and no position can be sourced.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Robespierre held that formal political rights meant little without limits on wealth and provision for the poor; inferred from his property and taxation declaration.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The Convention was elected to draft a new republican constitution, and the 1793 Constitution was then put to a popular vote.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Revolutionary government suspended ordinary liberties for the Terror, and Robespierre defended it as necessary to secure the Republic.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Robespierre's declaration speaks of brotherhood among peoples, but this is not a doctrine of aid transfers; inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons are anachronistic; the emphasis on national defense and the levee en masse gives only an inferred lean toward self-reliance.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The 1793 Constitution had deputies chosen by direct male suffrage but the executive council chosen by the legislature, so direct election of a head of state is not stated; inferred from popular sovereignty.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banking as understood today did not exist, and the Convention directed assignats and the economy through the state, so independence from government is inferred as opposed.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: A historic-homeland claim is anachronistic, though the republic defended France's frontiers in war; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Robespierre's 1793 declaration limits property by the duty not to harm the rights of others and by the needs of society.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Anachronistic; Jacobins favored a republic of small property owners and the label has no place in their thought; inferred.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on it, and Jacobin public-good rhetoric neither favors nor opposes it.

collective-defense.rationale: The 1793 constitution stressed the fraternity of peoples and non-interference, and the Jacobins were wary of standing alliances; inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The 1793 constitution renounced conquest and respect for peoples' rights is inferred to cover annexation without consent, though the Republic annexed Belgium.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Jacobins subordinated the clergy to the state and attacked church property, while Robespierre kept a civic religion.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The Republic had no head of state, and the Jacobins were a political party leading the government; inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The Jacobins crushed the Federalist revolts and the Vendee to preserve the one and indivisible Republic.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Jacobinism is defined by centralisation and indivisible sovereignty, leaving no room for regional autonomy.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The Jacobins abolished the monarchy and executed the king.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Robespierre's declaration called for progressive taxation, the opposite of a flat tax.

character-from-environment.rationale: Robespierre's emphasis on public education and civic virtue rests on the view that institutions shape citizens.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Law was the expression of the general will and rulers were bound by it, though revolutionary government suspended the constitution.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Jacobin priority on public welfare and the Republic's wartime needs.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Indivisible popular sovereignty in a single assembly rejects blending powers between few and many.

leader-cult.rationale: Robespierre denounced individual idolatry, though the Jacobins did honor martyrs and a civic cult.

equal-parenting.rationale: Anachronistic; the Jacobins did not address custody, and inferred stances are split.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: An anachronistic Marxist-Leninist idea; inferred from the Jacobins' civic republicanism and unity of the people.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred from Robespierre's limits on property and wealth for the public good; not a stated land program in these sources.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from the Reign of Terror's hostility to emigres, which treated those who fled as enemies.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The 1793 constitution renounced conquest and stressed brotherhood of peoples; inferred, though the war led to annexations.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred from the 1793 declaration and constitution's freedom of worship, which excludes punishing conversion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from the republican and civic-virtue emphasis on law over dress codes.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred from national sovereignty and the assignat; the issue did not arise.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The Jacobins stressed a single French nation; inferred from their indivisible republic.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Jacobinism meant an indivisible, centralised republic with no separate self-governing national institutions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from their universal declaration of rights as the basis of equal citizenship.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The Jacobins stressed virtue and political morality as the spur of the Republic; inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: Inferred from the price maxima and measures against hoarding as wartime controls on economic power.

no-bailouts.rationale: Never addressed; the Committee of Public Safety did not pose the question.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The general will, the 1793 referendum and popular sovereignty put majority will above other institutions.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The Jacobin Club and the republic excluded women from political life.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Wartime controls and the levee en masse had autarkic features, but no stated policy of a closed bloc.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from their brotherhood of peoples; the Jacobins did not address trade standards.

moral-incentives.rationale: Robespierre made civic virtue and a sense of public duty the principle of the republic.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Jacobins sought mass popular revolution and levee en masse, not small armed vanguards; inferred.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Revolution abolished hereditary nobility and the Jacobins stood for equality of citizens.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Republican civic education centred on the French nation fits Jacobin nationalism; inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The 1793 declaration speaks of brotherhood of peoples and non-interference, though revolutionary war later spread French rule; inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: Jacobins promoted civic education, national festivals and the civic cults to instill republican virtue and patriotism.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Anachronistic; Jacobins stood for legal equality but did not address race-conscious policy.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed by the Jacobins; no basis for a position.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed by the Jacobins; no basis for a position.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Robespierre's declaration proclaims rights as universal to all peoples, not dependent on civilization.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Armies were subordinated to the Convention through representatives on mission; a political role for generals was feared.

paid-care-work.rationale: Care work was not addressed; the 1793 right to assistance does not settle it. Inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Republican virtue and civic morality stressed family duty; inferred from Robespierre's moral rhetoric.

office-by-exam.rationale: The 1793 constitution made officials elective and sovereignty popular; inferred rejection of exam-based appointment.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The wartime Republic controlled the economy in the public interest; state limits on foreign capital are inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The Revolution legalised divorce in 1792; adherence by Jacobins is inferred from that.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Popular sovereignty meant officials answerable to the people; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Anachronistic; private accounts conflict with the Republic's public-good and welfare principles.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Property was to serve the public good and be limited, but was not abolished; inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The National Convention held supreme, representative power in the Republic; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Jacobins pushed French as the sole language of the Republic against regional patois; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Defence of the Republic and national territory suggests restricting foreign landholding; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Jacobin universalism was formally colourblind and had no outcome-based concept; inferred, anachronistic.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Robespierre's republic of virtue opposed luxury and corrupting wealth.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The Republic sought to spread revolution abroad by supporting revolutionary movements; inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Jacobins championed the sovereignty of peoples, though they exported revolution; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Robespierre's attacks on the wealthy and on factions of money-power capturing the republic.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Jacobin suspicion of foreign plots and gold corrupting the republic, which the Terror treated as treason.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Not addressed; the Jacobins valued public assistance for families but no population policy is documented.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from the Jacobin commitment to an indivisible republic with one law and national citizenship, against local privileges.

job-guarantee.rationale: The 1793 Constitution declared public assistance a sacred debt, covering work for the able-bodied poor.

democratic-peace.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Robespierre's belief that free republics would bring peace and brotherhood among peoples.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Jacobins demanded obedience to the general will and the law, while keeping a right to insurrection against tyranny.

non-intervention.rationale: The 1793 Constitution renounced interfering in other nations' governments, yet the Jacobins fought a revolutionary war to spread liberty; the record is split.

industrial-unions.rationale: Anachronistic; the Jacobins banned guilds and workers' combinations under the Le Chapelier law tradition, so any union form is unlikely.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The Jacobins saw conspiracies by aristocrats, priests and foreign powers, but these were political rather than ethnic or religious minorities as such.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Revolutionary law made marriage a civil contract and allowed divorce, but did not abolish its legal standing; inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Anachronistic; Jacobin ideals of public virtue and open deliberation and sessions suggest support, though the Terror restricted the press.

local-production.rationale: Not addressed; the Maximum regulated grain across the nation, but no preference for local production is documented.

informal-organisation.rationale: The Jacobins were a disciplined national network of affiliated clubs and distrusted factions.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Indivisible national sovereignty was central, and the people's law was held to override any outside authority.

religious-nation.rationale: Robespierre's Cult of the Supreme Being was civic rather than confessional, and the republic defined citizenship by civic virtue, not a shared church.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from the Jacobin ideal of a brotherhood of peoples and sovereign equality of nations, which rejects tribute and submission.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Jacobins held the republic one and indivisible and treated federalism as a Girondin threat, so regions would not keep their own revenue.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Robespierre limited property and taxed wealth progressively but defended private ownership, so he would not extend common ownership to production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Anachronistic: Jacobins defended private property and fought foreign monarchies, not communism; inferred from their property stance.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The 1793 Constitution made public assistance a state duty; inferred that provision would be run by the state, not private bodies.

religion-illusion.rationale: Robespierre denounced atheism and promoted a civic cult of the Supreme Being, treating religion as socially useful, not an illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Anachronistic: Jacobins favoured small property and price maxima, and no stance on capitalism as a historical stage is documented; inferred as split.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Jacobins excluded women from political rights and clubs; no economic account of women's subordination is documented. Inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: The Constitution made public assistance and education a duty, but domestic work was left to families; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Jacobins pushed French over regional languages, but no stance on purging foreign loanwords is documented. Inferred as split.

treaties-binding.rationale: With sovereignty one and indivisible, there are no internal nations with treaty standing; the state may change its own laws.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred: a centralised republic of citizens leaves no room for self-governing communal societies holding property in common.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from their forced assimilation of regions to a single French nation, but settlement policy is not documented.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Robespierre's limits on property and wealth with no abolition of ownership is arguably a third course, though the framing is anachronistic.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred: the 1793 declaration and the brotherhood of peoples rest on universal rights, not ancestral priority, though the Jacobins also claimed France's 'natural frontiers'.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Anachronistic: the Jacobins predate the Holocaust by 150 years, and no position can be sourced.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The 1791 revolutionary penal code dropped sodomy as an offence, but Jacobin moralism and the Year II republic of virtue were hostile to it, so adherents were not strongly against criminalisation.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Law of Suspects and the Terror suppressed opponents and clubs to defend the republic, and Robespierre justified terror as virtue's emanation.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The Jacobins pursued dechristianisation and a civic cult of the Supreme Being while the Constitution of 1793 guaranteed worship; punishing blasphemy in favour of a religion was not their aim.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred: the Convention abolished slavery in the colonies in 1794 and declared them part of France, which fits equal rights better than pure extraction.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The Jacobins did not address Islamic doctrine; their own analogue was the levee en masse for national defence, but this statement is out of scope.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: Jacobins founded legitimacy on popular sovereignty and secular virtue, so they would reject religious law as a test for removing rulers.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The Jacobins backed popular sections, political clubs, and the Constitution of 1793's referendum and universal male suffrage, though revolutionary government centralised decisions.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Anachronistic: the Jacobins treated class and rights universally but excluded women from political rights, and the framework is modern.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic: inferred from the Jacobin Club's exclusion of women and its moralism, with no sourced position on gender identity.

assisted-dying.rationale: Anachronistic: inferred from Robespierre's moral and civic virtue ethic, with no sourced position.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Inferred: Jacobins fought Girondins and royalists as enemies of the republic, and the Left and Right in the National Assembly originated in their era.

alienated-labor.rationale: Anachronistic: the Jacobins sought property for all and limits on great wealth but did not analyse alienation, and Marx postdates them.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed in the Jacobin sources.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Robespierre's declaration placed sovereignty in the people, and the Jacobins rejected the divine right of kings.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred: the Jacobin dechristianisation campaign and civic cults pushed religious symbols from public life, but no sourced rule on dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed by any Jacobin source.

social-market-economy.rationale: Jacobins accepted private property and a market with price maxima and relief, resembling neither laissez-faire nor a modern social market; the match is loose.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The Jacobins organised the levee en masse and a citizen army to defend the republic.

rich-first.rationale: Robespierre's declaration limited property by its social usefulness and favoured progressive taxation, rejecting letting some grow rich while others wait.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred: the 1793 constitution declares non-interference in other nations, but the republic was at war with a coalition of monarchies and bloc politics did not exist.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The Jacobins overthrew the monarchy and rejected hereditary privilege; popular sovereignty excludes inherited office.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred: Robespierre favoured public control over wealth but the sources do not address mutual credit.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from their hostility to financiers and their emphasis on national sovereignty; anachronistic for IMF-type lenders.

property-franchise.rationale: Robespierre condemned the property-based franchise and the Constitution of 1793 established universal male suffrage.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The Jacobins excluded women from political rights and shut women's clubs in 1793; the ecofeminist concept is anachronistic.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept, anachronistic; inferred from their civic-virtue ideal of a republic ruled by citizens, not by economic forces.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Robespierre argued that property must serve the public good and criticised the privileged rich; inferred as agreement with the thrust.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The revolutionary government of 1793-94 ruled by emergency decrees and the Law of Suspects, setting aside ordinary standing-law constraints.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Jacobin conception of equal citizenship and the 1793 constitution rejected restricting political rights to a group; abolition of slavery in 1794 followed this.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from their ideal of active, direct citizen participation in a republic.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from Robespierre's stress on public transparency and publicity of government as a republican virtue.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The Revolution secularised marriage as a civil contract; Jacobin republicanism opposed religious legal distinctions.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred from universal equal citizenship; the sources do not discuss consumer boycotts.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Jacobins placed sovereignty in the elected National Convention and primary assemblies, so decision by lot is inferred to be unfamiliar to them.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Robespierre rejected Church authority and promoted a rationalist Cult of the Supreme Being; applying this to religious doctrine is an inference.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Robespierre's 1793 declaration made property subordinate to the public good and condemned extreme inequality of fortune as a threat to republican liberty.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the 1791 decriminalisation of sodomy and the Jacobin emphasis on equal citizenship.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Robespierre opposed the dechristianisation campaign and instead set up the Cult of the Supreme Being, so the state promoted a civic deism, not atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The Jacobin republic relied on policing, revolutionary tribunals and imprisonment of suspects as core instruments of the Terror.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Sovereignty was held to be one and indivisible, which excludes guaranteed shares of power for particular communities.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The 1793 Constitution made public assistance a sacred debt of society, placing relief of the poor on the state rather than on charity.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred from Robespierre's push for non-re-eligibility of the Constituent Assembly deputies and from the 1793 Constitution's short, frequently renewed mandates.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred: the 1793 Constitution relied on direct popular ratification of laws and elected deputies, not delegable, revocable proxy voting.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic; the Jacobins had no concept of extinction-risk policy, so nothing can be inferred either way.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from Jacobin anticlericalism and the 1793 closure of women's political clubs; no stance on women's religious office is documented.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Revolutionary law introduced divorce and equal inheritance, but Jacobins kept women out of political life, so adherents' views were mixed; inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The 1793 Constitution admitted resident foreigners to citizenship after a year, which suggests openness to resident foreigners' participation; inferred and anachronistic for a local vote.

rent-control.rationale: The Montagnard government imposed the General Maximum on prices in 1793-94 and subordinated property to public need, which suggests support for price controls.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not an issue for them; inferred from a property-friendly stance and the 1791 revolutionary-era author and invention rights that they continued.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Revolutionary republican education sought to form young citizens through civic festivals, the Ecole de Mars and youth battalions; inferred, with the drilled element only partly documented.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic: nuclear weapons did not exist, and no principle clearly decides it.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from the demand for indivisible national sovereignty, which treats foreign armies on French soil as incompatible with it.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Anachronistic: the concept of genocide did not exist, though the Convention did call the Vendee war a crime against the nation.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Robespierre held that property must serve the public good and that society owes subsistence to citizens, rather than rewarding mere wealth.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The Jacobins defended the republic by terror and Robespierre made virtue and terror joint principles, so killing for the public good was justified.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Jacobins saw the Revolution as a rupture with the old regime and a re-founding of the nation, not a continuous ancient identity; inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Enlightenment natural-rights thinking, which saw sex differences as nature and not social products.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: The Jacobins excluded women from political rights and closed women's clubs in 1793; inferred that they did not question the category.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The Jacobins honoured Marat, Le Peletier and Bara as martyrs of liberty with public cults; inferred from the revolutionary festivals rather than from the listed sources.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Robespierre's report presents politics as a moral contest between virtue and vice and he later established the Cult of the Supreme Being.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The Republic was one and indivisible and aimed to gather all French citizens, not to serve a scattered diaspora; inferred.

culture-before-state.rationale: The Jacobins sought to regenerate the people through the republican state and its institutions, so the state came first; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Anachronistic; the Jacobins' deism and Supreme Being did not specify gender, and no principle decides it.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Jacobin exclusion of women from political rights and hostility to clerical tradition.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from their egalitarian republic of all citizens; they did not set economic life aside for a national majority, but the question is anachronistic.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The Jacobins imposed uniform departments and opposed regional particularism and federalism in the name of an indivisible republic.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred: the Jacobin republic subordinated all bodies to the sovereign state, and the Le Chapelier ban on workers' associations was never repealed; not discussed in the sources.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Anachronistic inference: Robespierre's democracy puts the sovereign people, including the poor, above wealth, though not as a workers' state.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from the 1793 declaration's subordination of property to social utility and its right to public assistance.

second-chamber.rationale: The Constitution of 1793 vested legislative power in a single unicameral assembly, as the sovereign people's delegate.

municipal-property.rationale: Robespierre limited property and taxed wealth progressively but kept private ownership; no municipal ownership was proposed.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Jacobins were centralisers who attacked the Girondins as federalists and defended an indivisible republic.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from the right to subsistence and public assistance in Robespierre's declaration and the 1793 Constitution.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Anachronistic: the 18th-century Jacobins never addressed drug regulation, so there is nothing to infer from.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Anachronistic: not addressed; the Jacobin cult of progress and reason gives no clear direction.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred: the Terror's state surveillance and tight control of money and prices leave no room for untraceable payments.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the Terror's denunciation, Law of Suspects and demand for transparent civic virtue.

person-over-state.rationale: Robespierre held that virtue and terror served the republic and its people, so individuals could be sacrificed to the public good.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Robespierre promoted the civic Cult of the Supreme Being and the immortality of the soul as moral foundations of the republic.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The republic was one and indivisible and departments were agents of the Convention, which could override them.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic: not addressed, and nothing in Jacobin principles bears on it.

dense-cities.rationale: Anachronistic: not addressed; no stated position on city density.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred from the universal rights of man, brotherhood of peoples and the 1794 abolition of slavery; racial groups were not political units.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from the universalist stress on shared citizenship and brotherhood of peoples rather than racial identity.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Contested: the 1793 Constitution rejects conquest, yet the Jacobin republic waged revolutionary war and levée en masse.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The nation was the citizenry of the one republic and not an ethnolinguistic group, though the Jacobins pushed French as the national language; inferred.

communal-electorates.rationale: Indivisible sovereignty and a single body of citizens rule out separate religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Robespierre denounced foreign conspiracies and a foreign faction aiming to destroy the Republic, and the Terror targeted them.

free-public-college.rationale: The 1793 Constitution declared education a need of all citizens, which suggests public provision, but it addressed schooling and not colleges; inferred.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on pollution or resource pricing.

future-generations.rationale: Republican virtue and regeneration looked to posterity, but there was no ecological sense; inferred.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The Jacobin-led Convention closed women's political clubs in 1793, treating women's role as domestic; inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: The Jacobins mobilised the nation for war and the levee en masse, so disarmament was not their aim; inferred.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Robespierre favoured publicity in politics, but the Committee of Public Safety conducted foreign policy in secret; split and inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: The wartime republic controlled prices and trade and restricted specie, so state control of capital movements fits; inferred.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The Convention disarmed suspects yet championed an armed citizenry and revolutionary armies, so adherents are split; inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The republic fought a war of national defence and treated desertion and refusal of duty as treason against the patrie.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Combinations of workers were barred by the 1791 Le Chapelier law and the General Maximum capped wages; inferred.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Tax credits are anachronistic; the Jacobins backed progressive taxes and public assistance but no wage top-ups; inferred.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Wartime finance ran on assignats and requisitions with no legal borrowing cap; inferred from emergency practice.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Developing-country economic claims are anachronistic and the sources never address them; no clear inference.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The Jacobins built a more centralised state rather than dismantling it, though they had overthrown the monarchy; inferred.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The Jacobins favoured a uniform centralised republic and wartime economic controls over local experiments; inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Ecosystem valuation is anachronistic and was not discussed; no clear inference from principles.

sacred-nation.rationale: Robespierre made love of the patrie and the indivisible people central to republican virtue, and the Cult of the Supreme Being gave the republic a quasi-sacred character.

student-debt-relief.rationale: The 1793 Constitution recognised public assistance and education as social duties, so relief for graduates fits loosely; inferred.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Jacobins rejected federalism and regional particularism in the name of one indivisible republic; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The 1793 declaration grounds universal natural rights in human nature, though the Jacobins also sought to regenerate citizens through virtue.

public-service-media.rationale: The Terror suppressed hostile newspapers, so independent media free of government control did not fit the revolutionary government; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Robespierre's deist Cult of the Supreme Being treated religion as one civic moral truth; inferred from that cult.

farm-price-support.rationale: The maximum fixed grain prices in consumers' favour while the state also aided farmers, so no clear price-support stance; inferred.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the levee en masse and the insistence on defending the republic against rival powers.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Jacobin Club was a cross-class republican club, not a workers' party; inferred.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Robespierre's universal declaration of rights that bind every custom.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Revolutionary law equalised inheritance among children, though women were kept out of politics; inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Jacobins pushed French as the single national language yet treated regional speech as patois; no clear stance on naming.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a centralised state that limited property by the public good rather than private suits.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Indivisible popular sovereignty left no place for hereditary or customary authorities in lawmaking.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the subordination of private interest to the general good and civic virtue.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: The Law of 22 Prairial made death the fixed penalty for convicted enemies, showing preference for rigid severity.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the drive for a single French language and civic assimilation.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Le Chapelier-era hostility to corporate bodies and the Jacobin emphasis on the indivisible people.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred: the 1793 declaration and constitution made citizenship and the vote universal for men, with no ID regime.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Robespierre defended freedom of worship while promoting a civic Cult of the Supreme Being; inferred.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Robespierre held that government in crisis rests on virtue and terror, not only on elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: Robespierre's moralism and civic virtue suggest disapproval; inferred.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the Terror's emergency measures, including censorship and surveillance, to protect the republic.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Anachronistic; the Jacobins favoured public relief and a right to subsistence, not a cash substitute.

women-suffrage.rationale: The 1793 Constitution gave the vote to men only, and the Jacobin-led Convention closed women's political clubs in 1793.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from Jacobin anticlericalism and de-Christianisation, though Robespierre opposed atheism.

race-social-construct.rationale: The Jacobins' universalist rights declaration and 1794 abolition of slavery imply a rejection of racial hierarchy; inferred.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Jacobin view of women's place in the domestic sphere.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Robespierre's 1793 declaration defines property by law and limits it by its duty to society, rejecting an absolute first-claim right.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its insistence on national sovereignty and its revolutionary suspicion of outside judgment.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Jacobins favoured a deist civic cult of the Supreme Being and dechristianisation pressures over revealed, literal religion.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Anachronistic; women were excluded from political rights and clubs, so guaranteed gender equality is not a Jacobin aim.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its defence of private ownership and its republican, not collectivist, economy.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred: the 1793 Constitution relied on direct popular election and referendum, though some offices were chosen through electoral assemblies.

national-church-status.rationale: The Jacobins opposed a privileged church and promoted a state civic religion instead of the traditional national church.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The republic was one and indivisible and the Jacobins crushed federalism, so territorial autonomy was rejected.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from popular sovereignty; the sources do not discuss plebiscites on territory and annexations were contested.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Anachronistic; the sources do not address colonial borders and indivisibility points both ways.

simple-living.rationale: Robespierre made civic virtue, frugality and austerity the basis of the republic.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its centralised, uniform republic that did not make regional carve-outs.

equal-conscription.rationale: The levee en masse called up men, and women were excluded from arms and political clubs.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The levee en masse and cult of the patrie show deep attachment to defending the nation's soil, though not framed as ancestral or spiritual; inferred.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Not about drugs; the Terror used revolutionary tribunals and the Law of Suspects rather than killing without any process, though the line was thin.

close-ties-china.rationale: Anachronistic; the question has no counterpart in 1793-94.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The 1793 declaration speaks of brotherhood of all peoples, not kin-based protection; inferred.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Robespierre made property subordinate to the common good and the right to existence, which suggests a duty to others; inferred.

self-ownership.rationale: The 1793 declaration of rights treats liberty and security of the person as natural rights; inferred.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The sources do not address consumption taxes; no clear inference.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The 1793 constitution made public assistance a sacred debt but the sources do not say whether to target or universalise.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Jacobins denounced factions yet organised through their own club and committees; adherents' view is mixed.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Jacobins attacked speculators and hoarders and imposed the maximum, opposing monopolistic privilege.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The Jacobin Club was republican and secular, promoting a civic cult of the Supreme Being above confessional division.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The Jacobins looked to civic virtue and classical models; inferred that technology was not tied to ancestral values.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Revolutionary law allowed divorce on equal terms for either spouse, though the sources here do not address it; inferred.

national-resource-control.rationale: Revolutionary centralism asserted national sovereignty over resources; inferred.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Robespierre held that property is limited by the duty to society and that extreme inequality is incompatible with republican liberty, so process alone does not justify a fortune.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: The Jacobins did not address such a tax; they fought speculators and imposed the Maximum, but a modern levy is an anachronism.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Racism as a modern category was not discussed; inferred from the Jacobin 1794 abolition of slavery, which treated racial hierarchy as a live injustice.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Robespierre's declaration grounds law in justice and natural right, implying an unjust law lacks authority, though in power the Jacobins enforced law strictly; inferred.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Jacobin civic republican praise of virtuous labour and work as the basis of citizenship.

multipolar-world.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from revolutionary France's universalist claim to lead the free peoples against the monarchies of Europe.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The Jacobins predate Marx and held a petty-proprietor republican view of property, not a labour theory of value; inferred.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Jacobin patriotism was bound to the sans-culottes and the people, and the levee en masse defended the republic of ordinary citizens.

material-over-identity.rationale: The question is anachronistic; the Jacobins pursued both social-economic measures and civic or moral regeneration, so no clear ranking can be drawn.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Anachronistic; the Jacobins ran a controlled wartime economy with price maxima and were suspicious of free markets, and no communist party existed.

missingStatements.text: In a national emergency, a government may suspend ordinary legal protections to defeat its internal enemies.
missingStatements.rationale: The Law of Suspects and Revolutionary Tribunal suspended ordinary protections, and Robespierre defended terror as prompt, severe justice.

missingStatements.text: Governments should fix maximum prices for essential foods in times of scarcity.
missingStatements.rationale: The Law of the General Maximum fixed grain and staple prices, enforced by revolutionary armies.

notes: Jacobins were pragmatic on economics: generally pro-market in principle but driven to controls by war. Many answers are low-confidence inferences.
